Oliver Grant: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime Q&A. A few concise clarifications about kernel rollout cadence, batching presets for new apps, and cache pin semantics.

Priya Desai: I'll take kernel + cache. Maya can confirm timeline; Sam can add batching notes.

Oliver Grant: 1) Kernel rollout: will we offer tenant-level opt-in or only per-region toggles?

Maya Torres: Tenant-level opt-in planned. Console will have both per-tenant and per-region canary toggles. Global default flip only after at least two region canaries and a 48h stability window. No silent upgrades.

Oliver Grant: 2) Batching presets: should new projects default to 20ms or 50ms?

Sam Patel: Console presets will default new orgs to "interactive (20ms, target_tokens=64)". We'll surface a "cost" preset (50ms, 512 tokens) and an "adaptive" opt-in.

Oliver Grant: 3) Cache pin semantics: can customers pin specific conversation IDs? Any limits?

Priya Desai: Yes, API flag `cache.pin=true` supported per-session. Default pin quota per-tenant is 2000 pinned keys; tenants can request increases. Pinned items bypass soft TTL and are only evicted under severe memory pressure.

ops-bot: Created task runtime/CANARY-119 to publish per-tenant opt-in docs (owner: Maya).

Maya Torres: Actionables: I'll post the rollout timeline + Console mock for the canary toggle by EOD, Priya will add cache.pin examples to docs, Sam will publish batching presets rationale.

Oliver Grant: Thanks all, I'll add these to the all-hands recap and tag owners. :thumbsup:
